items.title: Django UrlConf Checks
items.text:
Static checker that keeps your URL patterns and view annotations in sync, using Django’s built-in check framework.

The checker follows Django's resolver argument passing for path(), re_path(), nested include() calls, converter and regex captures, positional regex groups, and URL pattern keyword arguments.

For class-based views, it checks the methods selected by as_view() and DRF ViewSet actions, including handlers inherited from user base classes. It uses the same route arguments for each handler. The W001 star-argument warning is not emitted for class-based view handlers because *args and **kwargs are normal in Django generic views.

  • Documentation
  • GitHub
  • PyPI

items.title: Key features
items.text:
• Detects mismatches between URL converters/default kwargs and view annotations (ints, UUIDs, container generics, etc.).
  • Works as a Django system check (manage.py check) or standalone CLI.
  • Honors custom converters and fine-grained silencing per view.
  • Pre-commit friendly; CI-ready with machine-readable output.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
pip install django-urlconfchecks

Compatibility:

Python Django 3.11 5.2 3.12–3.15 5.2, 6.0, 6.1

Supported Python versions follow the Python release cycle: versions are dropped once they reach end-of-life. Django has no upper bound, so new releases install without waiting for a package update.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
1) Install: pip install django-urlconfchecks 2) From your project root (where manage.py lives): urlconfchecks * Or target a specific module: urlconfchecks --urlconf myproj.urls 3) Optional: add defaults in pyproject.toml:

[tool.urlconfchecks]
quiet = true
format = "json"
silenced_views = { "myproj.views.legacy_view" = "E002" }

CLI flags always override these defaults.

items.title: As a Django app
items.text:
Add django_urlconfchecks to your INSTALLED_APPS list in your settings.py file.

    INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    'django_urlconfchecks',
]

items.title: As a command line tool
items.text:
Run this command from the root of your project, were manage.py is located:

$ urlconfchecks --help

    Usage: urlconfchecks [OPTIONS]

      Check all URLConfs for errors.

    Options:
      --version
      -u, --urlconf PATH    Specify the URLconf to check.
      -q, --quiet           Suppress human-readable output; exit codes still set.
      -f, --format TEXT     Output format. Supported: json.
      --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
      --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or
                            customize the installation.
      --help                Show this message and exit.

items.title: As a pre-commit hook
items.text:
Add the following to your .pre-commit-config.yaml file:

  - repo: https://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks
    rev: v0.17.0
    hooks:
      - id: django-urlconfchecks

For more information, see the usage documentation.

The usage documentation also includes a ready-to-copy VS Code task.

items.title: What it catches (example)
items.text:
# urls.py
from django.urls import path

from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('articles/<str:year>/', views.year_archive),
    path('articles/<int:year>/<int:month>/', views.month_archive),
    path('articles/<int:year>/<int:month>/<slug:slug>/', views.article_detail),
]

# views.py


def year_archive(request, year: int):
    pass


def month_archive(request, year: int, month: int):
    pass


def article_detail(request, year: int, month: int, slug: str):
    pass

Output:

(urlchecker.E002) For parameter `year`, annotated type int does not match expected `str` from urlconf

JSON (--format json):

{
  "errors": [
    {
      "id": "urlchecker.E002",
      "message": "View myproj.views.year_archive for parameter `year`, annotated type int does not match expected `str` from urlconf",
      "obj": "<URLPattern 'articles/<str:year>/'>",
      "hint": null
    }
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "total_errors": 1,
  "total_warnings": 0
}

The checks include type mismatches (E002 and E005), missing or unexpected view arguments (E003, E004, and E006), too many positional regex arguments (E007), a parameter receiving both a positional URL value and a keyword argument (E008), and warnings for star arguments (W001 on function views), unknown converter output types (W002), missing annotations (W003), and optional regex groups without a view default (W004).

Use URLCONFCHECKS_SILENCED_VIEWS for fine-grained silencing. Class-based view handler errors use names such as my_project.views.ArticleView.get; my_project.views.ArticleView.* matches all handlers, and my_project.views.ArticleView matches the whole class. Function-view names keep the existing behavior.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:

items.text: • Handle cases involving path and include. Courtesy @spookylukey

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Python 3.12 support
  • Django 5 support

items.title: Removed
items.text: • Python 3.7 support

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Added python 3.13 and 3.14 support.
  • CLI now supports --format json to emit structured results with per-type counts and totals.
  • CLI gains --quiet / -q to suppress normal output while preserving exit codes and summaries.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Dropped python 3.9 support
  • Project tooling now uses uv for syncing/building and Ruff for linting/formatting (pre-commit and CI).
  • Raised the minimum supported Django version to 4.2 (with targeted upper bounds per Python release).
  • Improved type compatibility checks for typing.Annotated, Optional, and Union, and cache URL converter lookups for faster runs.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Custom boolean path converters are recognized and validated alongside the built-ins.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Parameterized generics validation: lists, tuples (fixed/variadic), dicts, sets, and optional containers are now type-checked against URL converters and default kwargs.
  • Pyproject configuration: [tool.urlconfchecks] supports defaults for quiet, format, and silenced_views, with URLCONFCHECKS_PYPROJECT override; custom silencers merge with built-ins.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Container type checking now reports mismatches instead of silently passing parameterized generics.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Handle functools.partial callbacks in _make_callback_repr for Django Ninja or similar frameworks. thanks @joseanoxp

items.title: Changed
items.text: • Updated the supported version matrix to Python 3.10-3.14 with Django 5.2 and 6.0.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Resolved false URL signature type mismatches when views or custom converters use from __future__ import annotations.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Support for Django 6.1 and Python 3.15.
  • Weekly CI job testing against Django's development branch.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Removed upper bounds on Python, Django and typer so new releases install without waiting for a package update.
  • Supported Python versions now follow the Python release cycle; versions are dropped at end-of-life.
  • Bumped development and test dependencies to their latest versions.

items.title: Removed
items.text: • Python 3.10 support (end-of-life since 2026-10-01), and the tomli dependency it required.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Class-based views are checked: each Django/DRF handler (get, post, …, an overridden dispatch, an explicit head) and DRF ViewSet action is checked against the URL's arguments, including handlers inherited from user mixins. Silence them as module.View.get, module.View.* or module.View.
  • re_path() views are checked: named groups as str keyword arguments, unnamed groups as positional arguments.
  • urlchecker.E007 for URLs that pass more positional arguments than the view accepts, and urlchecker.W004 for parameters fed by an optional regex group without a default.
  • VS Code usage documentation, including a ready-to-copy task (#186).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Views with *args or **kwargs still have their named parameters checked (types, and required parameters without a URL source); this can report additional true positives alongside W001.
  • urlchecker.W001 is no longer emitted for class-based view handlers, where *args/**kwargs are idiomatic.
  • Replaced bump2version with bump-my-version in the development tooling.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• CLI flags (--format, --quiet, …) silently failed with exit code 1 in projects detected via manage.py, because they were passed on to Django's own command line.
  • --urlconf could not import modules from the current directory when run via the installed urlconfchecks command.
  • include() extra kwargs are passed to child views, and named groups captured by a regex parent reach path() children (both were false E004 errors).
  • A path() default that overrides a captured value is checked as that default only (previously a false E006).
  • W002 is emitted at most once per untyped converter class.

items.title: Added
items.text: • urlchecker.W005 when a view's signature can't be inspected; the check no longer crashes on such callbacks.

items.title: Changed
items.text: • urlchecker.W001 (view takes *args/**kwargs) is reported once per view instead of once per route, with the number of routes using it, and a hint to use functools.wraps in decorators or silence third-party wrappers. On real projects this cut W001 from 321 to 14 warnings (pretix), 243 to 7 (django-allauth) and 103 to 8 (wagtail bakerydemo).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
Found by differential fuzzing against Django's resolver and by running the checker on large open-source projects:

  • The check could crash on callbacks with a broken __signature__, __module__ or __qualname__, and on converters whose to_python isn't a callable.
  • URL keyword arguments are no longer matched to positional-only parameters (def view(request, pk, /)), which Django can't fill by keyword.
  • request must be receivable positionally: def view(*, request) and def view(**kwargs) now get E001.
  • A first parameter not named request (def view(req, **kwargs)) was reported as missing a value (E004), and positional regex values were mapped onto it.
  • Class-based views: an overridden setup() is checked like dispatch(); staticmethod/classmethod handlers are checked instead of skipped; callable objects used as handlers keep their first parameter.
  • Literal, NewType and TypeVar annotations are compared by their underlying types instead of always mismatching.
  • Named groups inside a negative lookahead/lookbehind are not treated as captured.
  • The CLI now runs manage.py the way python manage.py does when looking for the settings module. Projects whose manage.py sets DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE only under if __name__ == "__main__": without a main() function (healthchecks, netbox, paperless-ngx and many others) failed with ImproperlyConfigured.
  • When the settings module can't be found, the CLI prints a short message suggesting DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE or --urlconf instead of a traceback.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Maintained differential, robustness, and stress fuzzing tools in tests/fuzz, with a weekly workflow and a tox -e fuzz entry point.
  • urlchecker.E008 when a parameter would receive both a positional value from the URL pattern (an unnamed re_path() group) and a keyword argument (a parent capture or extra kwarg) — Django raises "got multiple values for argument".

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • urlchecker.W004 is no longer reported for an optional regex group whose name a parent include() kwarg also supplies: when the group doesn't match, Django passes the include's value.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
You can set defaults for django-urlconfchecks in your pyproject.toml so teams don’t have to repeat CLI flags.

[tool.urlconfchecks]
# Suppress human-readable output; exit codes still reflect errors.
quiet = true

# Output format. Supported: "json" (default remains human output).
format = "json"

# Merge additional silencers with built-in defaults.
# Key: glob for view import path; Value: comma-separated error codes.
silenced_views = { "myproj.views.legacy_view" = "E002" }

Notes

  • CLI flags always win: urlconfchecks --quiet overrides quiet = false and vice versa.
  • You can point to a specific config file with URLCONFCHECKS_PYPROJECT=/path/to/pyproject.toml.
  • Built-in silencers (e.g., Django contrib views without type hints) stay active; custom silencers are merged.

items.title: Contributing
items.text:
Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every little bit helps, and credit will always be given.

You can contribute in many ways:

items.title: Report Bugs
items.text:
Report bugs at https://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks/issues.

If you are reporting a bug, please include:

  • Your operating system name and version.
  • Any details about your local setup that might be helpful in troubleshooting.
  • Detailed steps to reproduce the bug.

items.title: Fix Bugs
items.text: Look through the GitHub issues for bugs. Anything tagged with "bug" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

items.title: Implement Features
items.text: Look through the GitHub issues for features. Anything tagged with "enhancement" and "help wanted" is open to whoever wants to implement it.

items.title: Write Documentation
items.text: django-UrlConfChecks could always use more documentation, whether as part of the official django-UrlConfChecks docs, in docstrings, or even on the web in blog posts, articles, and such.

items.title: Submit Feedback
items.text:
The best way to send feedback is to file an issue at https://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks/issues.

If you are proposing a feature:

  • Explain in detail how it would work.
  • Keep the scope as narrow as possible, to make it easier to implement.
  • Remember that this is a volunteer-driven project, and that contributions are welcome :)

items.title: Get Started!
items.text:
Ready to contribute? Here's how to set up django-urlconfchecks for local development.

  1. Fork the django-urlconfchecks repo on GitHub.

  2. Clone your fork locally

    $ git clone git@github.com:your_name_here/django-urlconfchecks.git

  3. Ensure uv is installed (pip install uv).

  4. Install dependencies and create the virtualenv:

    $ uv sync --extra test --extra doc --extra dev

  5. Create a branch for local development:

    $ git checkout -b name-of-your-bugfix-or-feature

    Now you can make your changes locally.

  6. When you're done making changes, check that your changes pass the tests, including testing other Python versions, with tox:

    $ uv run --extra dev tox

Tox uses tox-uv and uv-managed Python interpreters, so uv can install missing Python versions needed by the local tox matrix.

  1. Commit your changes and push your branch to GitHub:

    $ git add .
$ git commit -m "Your detailed description of your changes."
$ git push origin name-of-your-bugfix-or-feature

  2. Submit a pull request through the GitHub website.

items.title: Pull Request Guidelines
items.text:
Before you submit a pull request, check that it meets these guidelines:

  1. The pull request should include tests.
  2. If the pull request adds functionality, the docs should be updated. Put your new functionality into a function with a docstring, and add the feature to the list in README.md.
  3. The pull request should work for Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15. Check https://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks/actions and make sure that the tests pass for all supported Python versions.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
$ uv run pytest tests

To run a subset of tests.

items.title: Fuzzing
items.text:
The maintained fuzzer in tests/fuzz compares URL signature checks with Django's resolver and Python argument binding. It also runs a hostile callback and converter corpus and measures flat and deeply nested URLconfs. The generator is shared with tests/test_differential.py, so a seed and a Hypothesis example use the same case shapes.

Run a seeded differential job and replay it later with the printed seed:

python -m tests.fuzz differential --seed 123 --cases 2000 --report fuzz.md
python -m tests.fuzz robustness
python -m tests.fuzz stress
tox -e fuzz

Omit --seed to choose a random seed; the tool prints it before any case runs. The differential command exits with status 1 for a checker crash or a mismatch. The robustness command exits with status 1 for any exception. The stress command reports timing, peak RSS, and deep-include comparison with Django. It flags a more-than-twofold increase in time per route.

The oracle excludes the name-only part of E001 for generated keyword-only or absent request forms. W001, W002, W003, and W005 are diagnostic warnings. W004 is a route flag because an optional capture can make a required parameter fail. DRF cases run when rest_framework is installed. A real mismatch must become a focused regression test in tests/test_fuzz_regressions.py before the fuzzer is changed.

GitHub Actions runs the differential, robustness, and stress modes every week. Use the workflow dispatch inputs to provide a seed or a different case count; the Markdown report is uploaded when it exists.

items.title: Deploying
items.text:
A reminder for the maintainers on how to deploy. Make sure all your changes are committed (including an entry in CHANGELOG.md). Then run:

$ uv run bump-my-version bump patch # possible: major / minor / patch
$ git push
$ git push --tags

GitHub Actions will then deploy to PyPI if tests pass.

items.title: Stable release
items.text:
To install django-UrlConfChecks, run this command in your terminal:

$ pip install django-urlconfchecks

This is the preferred method to install django-UrlConfChecks, as it will always install the most recent stable release.

If you don't have pip installed, this Python installation guide can guide you through the process.

items.title: From source
items.text:
The source for django-UrlConfChecks can be downloaded from the Github repo.

You can either clone the public repository:

$ git clone git://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks

Or download the tarball:

$ curl -OJL https://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks/tarball/master

Once you have a copy of the source, you can install it with:

$ pip install .

items.title: Usage
items.text: You can use this package in different ways:

items.title: As a Django app
items.text:
Add django_urlconfchecks to your INSTALLED_APPS list in your settings.py file.

    INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    'django_urlconfchecks',
]

Now, if there is any error, you can check it when you run python manage.py check or when your django server runs or reloads with python manage.py runserver.

The checker follows Django's resolver argument passing for path(), re_path(), nested include() calls, converter and regex captures, positional regex groups, and URL pattern keyword arguments. It also checks Django and DRF class-based view handlers, including inherited handlers and DRF ViewSet actions. urlchecker.E007 reports too many positional regex arguments, and urlchecker.W004 warns when an optional regex capture has no default in the view signature. urlchecker.W001 is reported for function views with star arguments, once per view (with the number of routes using it); Django and DRF handlers use star arguments without that warning. Most W001s come from decorators: wrap the inner function with functools.wraps and the checker sees, and checks, the decorated view's real signature. Silence third-party wrappers with a glob such as {"allauth.*": "W001"}.

The error codes are E001 (missing request parameter), E002 (converter type mismatch), E003 (missing URL parameter), E004 (required parameter without a URL source), E005 (extra argument type mismatch), E006 (unexpected extra argument), E007 (too many positional URL arguments), and E008 (a parameter receives both a positional URL value and a keyword argument). Warnings are W001 (star arguments on function views), W002 (unknown converter output), W003 (missing annotation), W004 (optional regex capture without a default), and W005 (view signature could not be inspected).

items.title: As a command line tool
items.text:
urlconfchecks uses the Typer module to parse command line arguments.

Run this command from the root of your project, were manage.py is located:

$ urlconfchecks --help

    Usage: urlconfchecks [OPTIONS]

      Check all URLConfs for errors.

    Options:
      --version
      -u, --urlconf PATH    Specify the URLconf to check.
      -q, --quiet           Suppress human-readable output; exit codes still set.
      -f, --format TEXT     Output format. Supported: json.
      --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
      --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or
                            customize the installation.
      --help                Show this message and exit.

--urlconf is optional, and if not specified, app will try to find the manage.py in your current directory for accessing the main URLConf module.

Example:

$ urlconfchecks --urlconf my_project.urls

  Done. No errors found.

items.title: As a pre-commit hook
items.text:
Make sure you have pre-commit installed and if not, install it with pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install.

Then, add the following to your .pre-commit-config.yaml file:

  - repo: https://github.com/AliSayyah/django-urlconfchecks
    rev: v0.17.0
    hooks:
      - id: django-urlconfchecks

Run pre-commit run to check all URLConfs for errors.

items.title: In VS Code
items.text:
The checks run as part of python manage.py check, so you can run that command from a VS Code task or terminal. You can also run the standalone urlconfchecks command. For example, save this as .vscode/tasks.json:

{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "Check URLConfs",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "urlconfchecks",
      "problemMatcher": [],
      "group": "test"
    }
  ]
}

The task leaves output in the terminal because the human-readable CLI output does not use a stable file:line:message format. The pre-commit hook above is also available for checks before each commit.

items.title: Configuration defaults
items.text:
You can set defaults in pyproject.toml so teams don’t repeat flags:

[tool.urlconfchecks]
quiet = true
format = "json"
silenced_views = { "myproj.views.legacy_view" = "E002" }

Notes:

  • CLI flags override these values.
  • Built-in silencers remain; custom entries are merged.
  • To point to a specific config file, set URLCONFCHECKS_PYPROJECT=/path/to/pyproject.toml.

items.title: Silencing errors and warnings
items.text:
You can silence specific errors and warnings as described in the System check framework documentation.

For example:

SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = [
    "urlchecker.W003“,
]

However, this turns off the check for all view functions. Instead of this you can use the URLCONFCHECKS_SILENCED_VIEWS setting for more fine grained silencing. The value must be a dictionary:

  • whose keys are fully qualified dotted paths to view functions or callables, with globbing syntax allowed, e.g. "my_project.views.my_view" or "other_project.*". For a class-based view, use a handler name such as "my_project.views.ArticleView.get", "my_project.views.ArticleView.*" for all handlers, or "my_project.views.ArticleView" for the whole class.

  • whose values are comma separated lists of warning or error IDs (without the urlchecker prefix), e.g. "E001,W003”

The default value of URLCONFCHECKS_SILENCED_VIEWS is below. If you override it in your settings.py, you will probably want to include the following and add more items:

URLCONFCHECKS_SILENCED_VIEWS = {
    "*.View.as_view": "W001",  # legacy/unresolved CBV callbacks
    "django.views.generic.base.RedirectView": "W001",
    "django.contrib.*": "W003",  # admin etc.
}
